# Appeal of Denied Prior Authorization — Request for Reconsideration

**Date:** [Date I am sending this letter]

**From:**
Quinn Ellison
Member ID: W391580594
[My mailing address]
[My phone number]

**To:** Aetna — Member Complaint and Appeal Unit
[Appeal address printed on my denial letter]
Fax: 859-425-3379

**RE: Appeal of adverse benefit determination dated 2026-08-04 — Reference number POC-DF42BEB029-97975**
**Member:** Quinn Ellison | **Member ID:** W391580594 | **Plan:** Aetna (Commercial/ACA), Montana
**Service denied:** Partial knee replacement, CPT 27446
**Governing policy:** Aetna Clinical Policy Bulletin 0660 — Knee Arthroplasty (https://www.aetna.com/cpb/medical/data/600_699/0660.html)

---

## Why I am writing

I am appealing the denial of prior authorization for a partial knee replacement (CPT 27446), which Aetna denied on 2026-08-04 under reference number POC-DF42BEB029-97975. The stated reason was that the imaging findings submitted do not support the medical necessity of the requested procedure.

I am asking Aetna to reconsider that decision. The imaging and records already in my file match the criteria in Aetna's own published policy, Clinical Policy Bulletin 0660 — Knee Arthroplasty. My surgeon, Lindqvist, MD, orthopedic surgery, has documented that this procedure is needed, and I would like a reviewer to compare the records to the policy language below.

## The plan's own criteria, and what my records show

**1. The policy's criterion for a partial (unicompartmental) knee replacement.**

CPB 0660 states:

> "Unicompartmental knee arthroplasty using Food and Drug Administration (FDA)-approved devices is considered medically necessary for members with advanced osteoarthritis or post-traumatic arthritis of the knee affecting only a single compartment (medial, lateral or patellofemoral), and who meet the following criteria (see also Additional Note ):"

The policy also states:

> "unicompartmental knee arthroplasty (UKA) is indicated when only 1 compartment is affected, and total knee arthroplasty (TKA) is indicated when 2 or 3 compartments are affected."

My imaging speaks directly to this point. The MRI of my knee dated 2026-05-28 showed full-thickness cartilage loss in the medial compartment with bone-on-bone apposition, and Kellgren-Lawrence grade 4 medially. That is advanced arthritis, and it is reported in a single compartment — the medial compartment. This is the exact clinical picture the policy describes as the indication for a unicompartmental, rather than a total, knee replacement. My physical exam also documents positive provocative testing on the affected side and range of motion limited by pain.

**2. The policy's conservative-therapy requirement.**

CPB 0660 states:

> "Members with osteoarthritis, traumatic arthritis, or avascular necrosis should have at least 12 weeks of non-surgical treatment documented in the medical record (at least 24 weeks for persons with a relative contraindication) - with at least half of the necessary conservative therapy consisting of formal physical therapy (in-person with a licensed physical therapist as opposed to home or virtual physical therapy) in the past year, including all of the following, unless contraindicated:"

My record documents more than the 12 weeks described:

- **Supervised, in-person physical therapy:** 16 weeks, from 2026-02-25 to 2026-06-17, with 24 visits completed, focused on quadriceps strengthening and range of motion. This is documented in the physical therapy discharge note.
- **Medication:** NSAIDs for 8 months, with inadequate relief.
- **Injection:** a corticosteroid injection on 2026-05-02, which gave about 4 weeks of partial relief.
- **Duration and course of symptoms:** 18 months of progressive knee pain, unrelieved by rest.

**3. Timing of the corticosteroid injection.**

CPB 0660 includes among its listed items:

> "or Corticosteroid injection into the joint within 12 weeks of the planned arthroplasty;"

My injection was given on 2026-05-02. [Planned or requested surgery date, if one has been scheduled — my surgeon's office can confirm.] I am noting the injection date here so the reviewer can confirm this point against the calendar rather than assume it.

**4. Impact on my daily life, and absence of contraindications.**

I cannot climb stairs without assistance, and I wake 3 to 4 times a night with pain. My record also documents no active infection, no untreated substance use, a BMI of 29, and that I am a non-smoker.

## In short

The denial rests on the imaging. The imaging is what most clearly supports the request: an MRI showing full-thickness cartilage loss with bone-on-bone apposition and Kellgren-Lawrence grade 4 changes, confined to the medial compartment — a single compartment, which is precisely what the plan's policy identifies as the indication for the partial knee replacement my surgeon requested. Alongside that, I completed 16 weeks of in-person physical therapy with 24 visits, 8 months of NSAIDs, and a corticosteroid injection, all documented in the record.

Where the policy language does not directly address a point, I have said so in plain prose rather than attributing words to the plan. Everything I have placed in quotation marks above is copied from CPB 0660 — Knee Arthroplasty.

## What I am asking for

I respectfully ask Aetna to overturn the denial dated 2026-08-04 (reference POC-DF42BEB029-97975) and approve prior authorization for CPT 27446. If the determination is not overturned, I ask that Aetna provide:

1. The specific criterion in CPB 0660 that my records were found not to meet, and the specific finding relied upon;
2. The credentials and specialty of the reviewer who made the determination; and
3. Written information about my right to further review, including external review.

I am submitting this appeal within the 180-day window stated in my denial notice, which gives a deadline of **2027-01-31**. I am sending it on Aetna's Member Complaint and Appeal Form (available in my account at aetna.com, under complaints, grievances and appeals), by fax to 859-425-3379 and/or to the appeal address printed on my denial letter. If anything further is needed from me or from Dr. Lindqvist's office, please contact me at the number above and I will provide it promptly.

Thank you for taking another look at this.

Sincerely,

**Quinn Ellison**
Member ID: W391580594
[Signature]
[Date]

**Enclosures:** [MRI report dated 2026-05-28]; [Physical therapy discharge note, 2026-02-25 to 2026-06-17]; [Office/operative planning notes from Lindqvist, MD]; [Copy of denial notice dated 2026-08-04]; [Medication and injection records]
